subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Reproduction (sexual/asexual, meiosis, DNA and the genome)
The development of our understanding of genetics and evolution

questions.q: How many cells does meiosis produce from one parent cell, and what are they like?
options: Two genetically identical diploid cells
Four genetically different haploid cells
Two genetically different diploid cells
Four genetically identical haploid cells
questions.explain: Meiosis produces four genetically non-identical gametes, each with half the normal chromosome number (haploid).

questions.q: How many chromosomes are found in a normal human gamete (sex cell)?
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying 23 single chromosomes, so fertilisation restores the full 46 (23 pairs).

questions.q: What is meant by the term 'genome'?
options: The entire genetic material of an organism
A single gene that codes for one protein
One pair of chromosomes in a body cell
The number of chromosomes in a gamete
questions.explain: The genome is all of the genetic material (DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the structure of DNA?
options: A single strand coiled into a sphere
A polymer made of two strands forming a double helix
A protein made of chains of amino acids
A carbohydrate storing genetic information
questions.explain: DNA is a polymer made from two strands coiled into a double helix and is contained in chromosomes.

questions.q: Who proposed the 'three-domain' system of classification (Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota)?
options: Carl Linnaeus
Charles Darwin
Carl Woese
Gregor Mendel
questions.explain: Carl Woese used evidence from RNA sequencing to divide organisms into the three domains: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota.

questions.q: In which year did Charles Darwin publish 'On the Origin of Species'?
questions.explain: Darwin published his theory of evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859.

questions.q: Which shows the correct order of the Linnaean classification groups, largest to smallest?
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Phylum, Kingdom, Order, Class, Family, Species, Genus
questions.explain: Linnaeus classified organisms into the hierarchy Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.q: In humans, which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a normal male?
options: XX
XY
YY
XO
questions.explain: Males have the sex chromosomes XY, while females have XX.

questions.q: Which set of features correctly describes asexual reproduction?
options: One parent, mitosis, genetically identical offspring
Two parents, meiosis, genetically varied offspring
One parent, meiosis, genetically varied offspring
Two parents, mitosis, genetically identical offspring
questions.explain: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and mitosis, producing genetically identical clones with no gamete fusion.

questions.q: Why is it important that gametes contain only half the normal number of chromosomes?
options: So the offspring grow more quickly than the parents
So the normal chromosome number is restored when two gametes fuse
So that each gamete can survive on its own
So that mutations can never be passed on
questions.explain: Halving the chromosome number in gametes means fertilisation restores the full diploid number in the new cell.

questions.q: A characteristic controlled by a recessive allele is only shown in the phenotype when the organism:
options: has one dominant and one recessive allele
has at least one recessive allele
has two copies of the recessive allele
has two copies of the dominant allele
questions.explain: A recessive allele is only expressed when it is homozygous, because a dominant allele would mask it.

questions.q: Which statement best describes evolution by natural selection?
options: Organisms deliberately change their bodies to suit the environment
Individuals best suited to the environment survive, reproduce and pass on their alleles
All individuals in a population reproduce equally regardless of their alleles
Characteristics gained during an organism's life are always inherited
questions.explain: Natural selection means the best-adapted individuals are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing on advantageous alleles.

questions.q: What does the process of selective breeding involve?
options: Inserting genes from one species into another
Choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together over generations
Producing genetically identical clones from one parent
Allowing only random mutations to determine offspring
questions.explain: Selective breeding (artificial selection) is humans choosing organisms with wanted characteristics and breeding them over many generations.

questions.q: Why can populations of bacteria become resistant to an antibiotic?
options: The antibiotic teaches the bacteria to change their DNA
A random mutation makes some bacteria resistant, and these survive and reproduce
All bacteria become resistant at the same time when exposed
Resistant bacteria are always produced by sexual reproduction
questions.explain: A chance mutation gives some bacteria resistance; these survive the antibiotic and reproduce, so resistance spreads through natural selection.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, which two groups are used to name an organism?
options: Kingdom and phylum
Genus and species
Class and order
Family and genus
questions.explain: The binomial system, devised by Linnaeus, names organisms using their genus and species.

questions.q: What did Gregor Mendel conclude from his breeding experiments with pea plants?
options: Characteristics are passed on by inherited 'units', now called genes
Acquired characteristics are always inherited by offspring
All variation is caused only by the environment
Living things were created in their present form
questions.explain: Mendel proposed that inheritance was determined by separately inherited 'units', which we now call genes.

questions.q: In pea plants tall (T) is dominant to short (t). Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed. What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring?
options: 1 tall : 1 short
3 tall : 1 short
1 tall : 3 short
4 tall : 0 short
questions.explain: A Tt x Tt cross gives genotypes TT, Tt, Tt, tt, producing a 3:1 ratio of tall to short.

questions.q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele (f). Two parents who are both carriers (Ff) have a child. What is the probability the child has cystic fibrosis?
questions.explain: An Ff x Ff cross gives a 1 in 4 (25%) chance of an ff child, who would have cystic fibrosis.

questions.q: A farmer breeds only her highest egg-laying hens together each year, and over several generations average egg production rises. This is an example of:
options: Natural selection
Selective breeding
Genetic engineering
Asexual reproduction
questions.explain: Humans choosing which organisms breed to increase a desired characteristic over generations is selective breeding.

questions.q: Scientists find that species A and species B share a much more similar DNA base sequence than species A and species C. What does this suggest?
options: A and C evolved more recently than A and B
A and B share a more recent common ancestor than A and C
The three species are equally closely related
A and C are the same species
questions.explain: More similar DNA base sequences indicate a closer evolutionary relationship and a more recent common ancestor.
